title: The Ottoman Empire's End as a Sequence
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: 四つの原文段落と全九つの学習対象を保持し、元の記述問題を英語四択へ変換しました。

passages.text:
The Ottoman Empire did not simply decline in a straight line from an early golden age. It repeatedly reformed taxation, the military, administration, education, and law while responding to internal disputes and changing relations with European powers. Reform could increase state capacity and also create new conflicts over citizenship, centralization, and local authority. Adaptation and crisis therefore coexisted.

During the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, nationalist movements, foreign intervention, fiscal pressure, territorial losses, and mass violence reshaped the empire. These forces did not operate independently, nor did they make every later border inevitable. People held overlapping religious, local, imperial, and linguistic identities. Reading the past only through the nation-states that later emerged turns uncertain choices into a predetermined map.

The First World War was a decisive acceleration. Ottoman defeat in 1918 was followed by Allied occupation and competing plans for partition. A Turkish nationalist movement then fought to establish a new center of sovereignty. The sultanate was abolished in 1922. The Treaty of Lausanne in 1923 recognized a new international settlement, and the Republic of Turkey was proclaimed that year. Defeat, abolition, treaty, and republic are connected, but they are not one event.

Nor was institutional succession a clean transfer. New states inherited populations, debts, railways, legal practices, and unresolved conflicts. War, forced migration, persecution, and population exchange transformed communities as well as borders. A careful history asks who gained authority, who lost protection or property, and which institutions continued under new names. “The end of an empire” is not a point; it is a sequence whose meaning depends on the scale of observation.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: The empire followed one uninterrupted decline that made all later borders inevitable.

options.label: B
options.text: The empire ended through a sequence of reforms, conflicts, defeat, abolition, settlement, and succession.

options.label: C
options.text: The treaty and the abolition of the sultanate were the same legal act.

options.label: D
options.text: New states inherited nothing from imperial institutions.

questions.answer: 正解：B。改革と危機、敗戦、制度廃止、条約、共和国、継承から成る連鎖が主題です。Aは直線的必然、Cは別の法的出来事の同一化、Dは継承の否定です。

questions.prompt: Why could reform increase both state capacity and conflict?

options.label: A
options.text: Centralized taxation, military, and education could improve implementation while disrupting local authority, citizenship, and existing communal arrangements.

options.label: B
options.text: Every reform removed all questions about rights and burdens.

options.label: C
options.text: Reform affected only foreign maps and never domestic institutions.

options.label: D
options.text: State capacity can grow only when administration is abolished.

questions.answer: 正解：A。制度統一は国家の実行力を高める一方、地方権限や共同体、市民権、負担配分を変えて対立も生みます。B～Dは改革の両面性に反します。

questions.prompt: The phrase “predetermined map” in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to

options.label: A
options.text: borders falsely treated as unavoidable from the beginning

options.label: B
options.text: a map printed before a train journey

options.label: C
options.text: a military order with no territory

options.label: D
options.text: a list of tax rates

questions.answer: 正解：A。後に成立した国境を最初から不可避だったかのように読む誤りを指します。Bは文字どおりの誤読で、CとDは国境と歴史的必然性の文脈を失います。

questions.prompt: What becomes difficult to see when imperial history is read only through later nation-states?

options.label: A
options.text: Overlapping local, religious, linguistic, and imperial identities and the uncertainty of alternative political arrangements

options.label: B
options.text: The certainty that every later border existed unchanged from the start

options.label: C
options.text: The absence of all local and religious identities

options.label: D
options.text: Proof that no alternative border or autonomy was ever possible

questions.answer: 正解：A。複数の帰属が重なる現実と、自治・連邦・国境の別の選択可能性が見えにくくなります。B～Dは後知恵による必然化そのものです。

questions.prompt: Which chronology is accurate according to the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: 1918 defeat and occupation process; 1922 abolition of the sultanate; 1923 Lausanne settlement and proclamation of the republic

options.label: B
options.text: 1918 proclamation of the republic; 1922 Treaty of Lausanne; 1923 Ottoman victory

options.label: C
options.text: 1918 abolition of the sultanate; 1922 Allied defeat; 1923 beginning of the First World War

options.label: D
options.text: All four developments occurred as one act on the same date

questions.answer: 正解：A。1918年は敗戦と占領過程、1922年はスルタン制廃止、1923年はローザンヌ条約と共和国宣言です。B～Dは年代・出来事を混同します。

questions.prompt: What does “connected, but they are not one event” mean?

options.label: A
options.text: The developments had no influence on one another.

options.label: B
options.text: One date is sufficient because military and legal change are identical.

options.label: C
options.text: The developments formed a sequence but involved different actors, processes, and legal meanings.

options.label: D
options.text: Only military history matters when sovereignty changes.

questions.answer: 正解：C。敗戦、制度廃止、国際条約、共和国成立は相互に関連しますが、主体・過程・法的意味が異なります。Aは関連を否定し、BとDは重要な区別を消します。

questions.prompt: Which group consists entirely of elements inherited by successor states?

options.label: A
options.text: Populations, debts, railways, legal practices, and unresolved conflicts

options.label: B
options.text: No people, property, infrastructure, or institutions

options.label: C
options.text: Only a new flag with no administrative continuity

options.label: D
options.text: Predetermined borders untouched by war or migration

questions.answer: 正解：A。人口、債務、鉄道、法慣行、未解決の対立などが継承されました。BとCは継続性を否定し、Dは戦争・移住による変化を無視します。

questions.prompt: What does it mean that the empire's end depends on the scale of observation?

options.label: A
options.text: A state may mark abolition as the endpoint, while a region may experience administrative continuity and a family may experience migration or property loss as the decisive change.

options.label: B
options.text: Every person and institution experienced one identical endpoint on one day.

options.label: C
options.text: Only international treaties count as historical change.

options.label: D
options.text: Individual and regional experiences cannot be studied historically.

questions.answer: 正解：A。国家・地域・家族では転換点が異なり、制度廃止、行政継続、移住・財産喪失など別の終焉を経験します。B～Dは尺度の違いを消します。

questions.prompt: Which museum design would best avoid reducing imperial dissolution to one date?

options.label: A
options.text: Use parallel timelines for defeat, institutions, treaties, and community change, and trace a town or family across contested borders.

options.label: B
options.text: Display only the final map and describe it as inevitable from the beginning.

options.label: C
options.text: Omit migration, violence, administration, and contemporary uncertainty.

options.label: D
options.text: Place defeat, abolition, treaty, and republic under one date without explanation.

questions.answer: 正解：A。複数の時間軸と同一地域・家族の追跡により、何が終わり何が続いたか、選択がどう争われたかを示せます。B～Dは一日・一地図へ還元します。
